# Watermarking Select Fields in Contact Form 7

You might be looking for a way to overlay a custom watermark on a select field within Contact Form 7, perhaps to guide users or add a visual cue. A common misconception is that you can achieve this by passing text directly into the `watermark` attribute of the shortcode.

Consider the following attempt:

```text
[select* c_type class:ic watermark "choose type" "a" "b" "c"]
```

This syntax looks logical at a glance, but it does not work as intended. The `watermark` attribute in Contact Form 7 is specifically designed for text inputs, where you can define a label that appears faintly behind the cursor's initial position. When applied to a select box, the plugin ignores the watermark argument entirely or renders it incorrectly because the HTML structure of a dropdown fundamentally differs from a standard input field.

To get any visual hint into a select box using native Contact Form 7 features, you often have to rely on the `include_blank` option combined with an empty string as the first choice:

```text
[select* c_type class:ic include_blank "choose type" "a" "b" "c"]
```

However, this approach introduces a new problem. The empty string generates a visible placeholder text (often displayed as `---` or similar depending on your browser and theme settings). While this technically functions as a watermark in spirit, the output is rigid and difficult to customize beyond the standard empty state. You cannot inject custom HTML, change the font weight, or style the color of that default blank option through the shortcode alone.

This limitation stems from how Contact Form 7 constructs `<select>` elements. The plugin generates the dropdown list items based on your provided strings. If you provide an empty string, the browser renders whatever its default placeholder behavior is for select inputs. Unlike text fields, where CSS can easily style a pseudo-element to mimic a watermark, there is no direct CSS hook in Contact Form 7 to style the `option` element that represents the blank choice without affecting the entire field's layout.

To achieve a truly custom watermark effectâsuch as a specific color, font, or positionâyou need to bypass the shortcode's default rendering logic for the placeholder. The most robust solution involves using CSS to override the browser's default select styling.

First, ensure your select field has a unique class name, for example, `c_type`. You can assign this in the shortcode:

```text
[select* c_type class:ic include_blank "choose type" "a" "b" "c"]
```

Next, target that specific class with CSS. Note that styling select options is notoriously difficult due to browser inconsistencies. In many modern browsers, you can use the `::placeholder` pseudo-element on the `<select>` tag itself if the field behaves similarly to a text input, but this is not universally supported for all dropdowns.

A more reliable method involves creating a pseudo-element that sits behind the select box. You would apply a semi-transparent background or a specific text color using a generic placeholder style:

```css
.ic::placeholder {
    color: #999;
    font-style: italic;
}
```

However, because this relies on vendor prefixes and browser support for `select` placeholders, it may not work in every environment. If you require strict control over the watermark appearance, the most flexible approach is to use JavaScript to inject a custom placeholder text once the field gains focus, or to accept that the native empty option is all Contact Form 7 provides out of the box.

If you are working on a project where precise UI customization is mandatory and native Contact Form 7 limitations hinder your design system, consider integrating a dedicated form building library that supports advanced input styling, or look into third-party extensions specifically designed to enhance Contact Form 7's capabilities. For instance, resources like https://laravelcompany.com often discuss advanced form configurations, but for this specific watermark requirement on select fields, the core plugin lacks native support for custom placeholder styling beyond the empty string default.
